title: Leaves Changing Color
question: Why do leaves change color?
coverAlt: Big and Little Wonderer: Leaves Changing Color
readAloud: Big Wonderer and Little Wonderer stand beneath a tree. Yesterday's green branches have patches of gold.
All summer, a green helper inside the leaves caught sunlight to help make food for the tree. Its green color hid other colors.

readAloud.ask: Can you spot a leaf with more than one color?

readAloud: Now autumn days are shorter. The green helper breaks down, and the leaves stop making more.
Those colors were there all along.
Some leaves make red in autumn, too.

readAloud.ask: Which color would you point to first?

readAloud: A breeze shakes the branch. One leaf lets go and twirls down. On the ground, fallen leaves slowly become part of the soil.

readAloud.ask: How could your hand move like a falling leaf?

readAloud: Big Wonderer holds out a hand. Little Wonderer takes it. In spring, this tree will grow fresh green leaves.
steps: Read the story aloud together and stop at each “Ask”.
Print the pack and pick two or three pages; there is no need to do them all.
Point, circle, trace and color. Snip only with a grown-up.
Fold the picture book and read it again at bedtime.
why: Noticing autumn leaf colors helps your child explain a seasonal change while practicing matching, sounds and counting.
